clue.text: Psycho killer rejected by mother

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the killer's name is read from its far end

blocks.note: MA is a familiar word for mother
Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis, the first murderer

explanation.surface: A murderous madman is spurned by his own mother, a nod to the Talking Heads song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Psycho killer' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'Psycho' is the definition and 'killer' is Cain. Mother comes first, with the reversed Cain after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A psycho is a dangerously deranged person, and a maniac is likewise someone wildly insane or violent.

clue.text: Traveller returning to embrace university sweetheart

indicators.note: returning means heading back the way it came, so the traveller is read upwards in this down entry
to embrace is to wrap arms around something, so one piece holds the other inside it

blocks.note: Roma are a traditionally travelling people
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A wanderer comes back to hug a college sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Roma are the Romani people, once often called travellers; their name turned round is AMOR, which wraps around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a borrowed French word for a lover or love affair, so it stands for a sweetheart.

clue.text: Frosty features in back room conservative institute

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the following three pieces are read upwards together

blocks.note: room in the sense of free space
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
I is the abbreviation for institute

explanation.surface: A back room at a Tory think tank has a chilly atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back room' looks like a single phrase, but 'back' reverses the whole string SPACE + C + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar ice caps are the frozen sheets crowning the poles, natural formations of ice on the globe.

clue.text: Nick some breakfast after emptying cereal

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outside letters
after tells us the breakfast item comes later than the cereal piece

blocks.note: the first and last letters of cereal
an egg is part of a breakfast

explanation.surface: Someone pinches part of a breakfast once the cereal bowl is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a verb meaning steal; it is the first name of Nick Clegg, Liberal Democrat leader and Britain's Deputy Prime Minister 2010-15.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Clegg is the British politician, so his first name points to his surname.

clue.text: Burning torch of unfinished passion pursued by lover

indicators.note: unfinished means the word stops short, losing its final letter
being pursued means something follows behind, so the lover piece comes second

blocks.note: a flame is a passion, as in an old flame
a beau is a boyfriend or admirer

explanation.surface: A smouldering, incomplete romance chased by an ardent lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning torch' sounds like a metaphor for love; here it is the literal object.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, especially one made of thick wicks dipped in wax, carried in processions.

clue.text: Very cold ales, for example - these may be offensive to some

definitions.text: these may be offensive to some

blocks.note: first meaning: very, cold and ales each have four letters, so they are examples of the kind

blocks.clueFragment: these may be offensive to some
blocks.note: second meaning: the euphemism for swear words, many of which happen to be short

explanation.surface: Some drinkers take offence at ice-cold beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a phrase about chilled beer; instead count the letters of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes words of four letters literally, and is also the polite label for crude swear words.

clue.text: People enjoying buzz in Paris as it bustles

indicators.note: something that bustles is all busy commotion, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Visitors love the buzz of Paris and its bustling streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enjoying buzz' sounds like city excitement, but the buzz is literal: bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiarists are beekeepers, people who tend hives and so spend their days amid buzzing insects.

clue.text: Ditch bar, Spooner advises sailor

indicators.note: Dr Spooner famously swapped the first sounds of words, so the opening sounds are exchanged

blocks.note: a moat is a defensive ditch and to ban is to bar; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A sailor is advised by Spooner to drop the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch bar' reads as advice to quit drinking, but both words are synonyms to be spoonerised.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman is someone who works on or handles boats, so is a kind of sailor.

clue.text: A growth that may become a tree

definitions.text: A growth that may become a tree

blocks.note: taken as written
a corn is a small hard growth of skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A seed or sprout described as a small growth that might one day become a full tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, while its first two words also build it: A plus a corn, the painful growth on a toe.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak, a seed that can sprout and grow into a full oak.

clue.text: Function of control experiment?

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters come from inside the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A scientist asks what a control experiment is for.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as lab science; the answer lies across the boundary of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is a job or purpose that something serves, the same as its function.

clue.text: Cryptic clue I'd plan around you, dear solver

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or encoded, so these letters are scrambled into a different order
turned around means facing the other way, so the schedule is read from its end

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
a rota is a plan of duties or shifts

explanation.surface: The setter addresses the solver about a cryptic clue they have planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic clue' is crossword talk, but 'Cryptic' is the anagram signal. A rota is a duty roster.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who elucidates makes a puzzle clear, which is exactly what a solver does when cracking a clue.

clue.text: A good trial run designed to get you to like nachos

indicators.note: something designed is deliberately arranged, so these letters are composed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A test run is planned to win someone over to nachos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like nachos' seems to mean being fond of them; it means resembling them in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Nachos are tortilla chips cut into three-sided wedges, so they are shaped with three corners.

clue.text: Short note that provides some cover for members

definitions.text: that provides some cover for members
definitions.note: a noun phrase for a skirt

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

explanation.surface: A brief memo explains how to protect the members of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' looks like club membership, but means limbs; a short skirt leaves the legs mostly bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniskirt covers only the top of the legs, giving those limbs a little covering.

clue.text: Extremely edgy books interrupting cycle of sleep

indicators.note: a cycle goes round, so the last letter of the nap word comes round to the front
interrupting means breaking into, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: NT is the New Testament, a collection of books
a siesta is an afternoon sleep

explanation.surface: Reading in bed disrupts sleep, leaving someone very jittery.
explanation.walkthrough: SIESTA with its last letter moved to the front becomes ASIEST, and the books go in after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Antsy is informal for restless or nervous, and the superlative means the most on edge.

clue.text: As woman was formerly known in topless joint

indicators.note: topless means with the top removed, and in a down entry that is the first letter

blocks.note: the knee is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: A woman's past is recalled in a seedy topless bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a club or bar, but it is a body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for born, introduces a married woman's maiden name, the name she formerly had.

clue.text: Crooks repeat experience turning over scam with shares, principally

indicators.note: turning means facing about, so the experience word is read backwards
lying over something covers it, so the scam ends up enclosed
principally means chiefly or first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to relive something is to experience it again
a do is a swindle in British slang
first letter of shares

explanation.surface: Fraudsters repeat a share scam, turning it over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reads as one phrase but does two jobs: 'turning' reverses, 'over' wraps around. A do is British slang for a con.
explanation.definitionFit: Evildoers are wrongdoers or villains, and crooks are dishonest criminals, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: A healthy look is fun not pain (some of the time)

indicators.note: only some of the time means intermittently, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: every second letter of the phrase, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Getting a healthy glow is fun, not painful, at least occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link word, but its S begins the alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tan from the sun gives skin a bronzed glow often thought to look healthy.

clue.text: Criminal law - that's boring

indicators.note: criminal means corrupt or wrong, so these letters are bent out of their proper order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that criminal law is a dull subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like tedious; it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool used to pierce holes in leather or wood, so it bores.

clue.text: Doctor one leads to Italian family

blocks.note: a medic is a doctor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A physician leads someone to an Italian family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medici were the powerful banking dynasty who ruled Florence during the Renaissance.

clue.text: Choose twelve people from a number in force

indicators.note: in places the number piece inside the force word

blocks.note: to impel is to force or drive
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Twelve people are selected from a number serving in a police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twelve people' is a jury: to impanel is to enrol jurors.
explanation.definitionFit: To impanel is to enlist a jury, and a jury is traditionally a panel of twelve people.

clue.text: Musicians in matching clothes

blocks.note: first meaning: a group of players performing together
second meaning: an outfit of coordinated garments

explanation.surface: A band performs dressed in coordinated outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the two meanings and is part of the surface picture of a band in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word names both a group of performers and an outfit whose pieces are designed to go together.

clue.text: One parting hurt such a relationship

definitions.note: describes the relationship, so the adjective fits

indicators.note: parting something splits it apart, so the single letter goes into the middle

blocks.note: marred means damaged or spoilt
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A separation damages a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parting' suggests a break-up; it is the container signal, with I splitting MARRED.
explanation.definitionFit: A married relationship is one between a wedded couple, so the word describes that kind of relationship.

clue.text: Give worker quiet warning

definitions.note: a noun, with 'Give' as the verb

blocks.note: a worker bee
p is piano, the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A manager quietly warns an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' suggests an employee; in crosswords it is often a bee.
explanation.definitionFit: A beep is a short electronic sound that serves as an alert, such as a horn or alarm.

clue.text: Flapper to feel bad after losing face

indicators.note: losing face means losing the front, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: to regret is to feel sorry about something

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper feels bad after being humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: A flapper suggests a jazz-age girl; here it is something that flaps its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron-like wading bird, and a bird flaps its wings, a whimsical name for it.

clue.text: Drink issue? That's coming later

blocks.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
to issue is to flow out, to stream

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether drinking will cause a problem, then is told it will come later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' reads as a problem, but it is the verb meaning to pour out.
explanation.definitionFit: Downstream describes stages that follow later in a process, as a river's lower reaches come after its source.

clue.text: Special promotion in hairstyles with male product

indicators.note: a promotion lifts something up, and in this down entry the end letter climbs to the top

blocks.note: perms are curled hairstyles

explanation.surface: A salon runs a special offer on hairstyles bundled with a men's product.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S of PERMS is moved to the top of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sperm is what the male reproductive system produces, so it is literally a male product.

clue.text: Seriously troubled, Dutch heartily gets stuck into a fresh escalation

indicators.note: heartily points to the heart, so only the central letter of the setter's name is kept
an escalation goes upwards, so in a down entry the word is read from the bottom
getting stuck into something means being lodged inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle letter of the setter's name
raw in the sense of fresh and uncooked

explanation.surface: The setter, troubled, gets heavily involved in a new escalation of conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is this puzzle's setter, signing his name into the clue. 'escalation' works upwards because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A country at war is in serious conflict, so the phrase means gravely troubled or in strife.

clue.text: Moving to a greener part of plantation

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone relocates to a greener corner of the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greener' suggests leafier countryside; it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus plantations are planted with rows of these fruit trees, so each one is part of the plantation.

clue.text: A succeeding island state?

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so the single letter is placed at the end

blocks.note: IOW is the abbreviation for the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether an island could thrive as an independent nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeding' hints at success; it means following on.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a state in the American Midwest, one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Takes drugs to suppress recall of current drunken exploits

indicators.note: a recall calls things back, so the following pieces are read backwards
suppressing something holds it down inside, so one piece contains the other

blocks.note: someone who takes drugs uses
I is the symbol for electric current
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drug user tries to hide the memory of their drunken escapades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploits' looks like a noun for escapades; it is a verb. 'recall' covers both current and drunken together.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it, and to utilise it is the same.

clue.text: New way to attract seamen

indicators.note: attracting draws something close, so the sailors' piece attaches to the end

blocks.note: a mode is a way or method
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A fresh approach for recruiting sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means of the present or recent times, hence new rather than old.
